title: Fire destroys the band's instruments; Trent's family buys new ones
summary: A fire burns all the instruments; Pillars borrows a horn for a gig and Trent's father buys everyone new instruments at the King factory.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: on the streetcar in front of my house. So this particular day I went down to go to work, and I walked in and there had been a fire. And I saw my beautiful saxophone all curled up where it was burned up. All the instruments were burned up. So that meant that Trent's band were locked in Cleveland, Ohio without instruments. So, we were exploited by two or three groups, they gave benefit dances for us, and we --when the dance was all over, when you checked to see how much money you had in the pot, you had none. So there was a boy in town named Jenkins, I can't think of Jenkins' name, first name, last time I saw Jenkins he was in Providence Rhode Island. I got a gig, Jenkins got a gig for me, he couldn't make it and he loaned me his horn. I made that gig, I made $16.00 on that gig. I was so happy to get that money, I didn't know what to do.

And we stayed in Cleveland that whole winter. Finally Alphonso Trent's father got together and took us out to the King Factory in Cleveland, Ohio, and they bought everybody an instrument. His father, his people put up the money and got everybody in the band an instrument. Now Spring of 1930. We started a tour and we booked into Columbus, Ohio, and we get to Columbus, Ohio and there was another band booked in there, Sammy Stewart's orchestra and that was Sammy Stewart's home, he was a Chicago band, and his band was playing a homecoming there.
